steps.title: Your name and your language
steps.body:
Forms in Canada ask for your nom and your prénom, and sometimes your language.

Nom is your last name. Prénom is your first name. They are easy to mix up, so we practise them.

steps.sound: noh (nasal, the same sound as non)
ka-na-DA (an even beat, a small lift at the end)

steps.prompt: Which word is your last name on a form?
steps.explain: Nom is your last name. Prénom is your first name.
Anglais means English. You say ahn-GLAY.

steps.prompt: You write Sam on a form. Which box is it?
steps.explain: Sam is a first name, so it goes in prénom.

steps.title: Same sound, different word
steps.body:
Non (no) and nom (last name) sound exactly the same. The m at the end of nom is not a separate sound. It only makes the o nasal.

You tell them apart from the situation: a yes or no question, or a form.

steps.question: Which word did you hear?
steps.explain: Prénom has two syllables: pray-NOH. Nom has only one.

steps.tip: The m in nom is not said. Say noh, with a nasal o.

steps.title: Unit 1 so far
steps.body:
You now know 10 words: bonjour, bonsoir, salut, oui, non, nom, prénom, français, anglais and Canada.

Next you learn the phrases you use to introduce yourself.
